universal._attendance_note: CHECK-IN COUNTS UNDERCOUNT ATTENDANCE. Not everyone who comes checks in -- attended.txt even records one guest who checked in under a different address than he bought under. So a figure higher than the check-in tally is NOT evidence of fabrication, and must not be reported as one. This file previously banned '28 attendees' as "unsourced" on exactly that mistaken reasoning, and the rule caused the same wrong conclusion to be re-derived more than once. run_of_show._comment: SETTLED 2026-09-01 by Taylor, against the shipped chemistry tool in public/admin.html rather than against any prose. There IS an icebreaker game and there IS a timer, and they are the same block -- the game is what you play at the tables. Every earlier description in this file and on the live site was wrong in one direction or the other -- see _what_was_wrong.
run_of_show._source: public/admin.html -- _tableSize, ROUND_CHOICES, _tableRounds, _roundMinutes, _oneOnOneMinutes, buildRunPlan(), and the host callout at 'women stay, men move one table along'. Read the code, not a summary, if this ever needs re-checking.

sequence.detail: 6:30. Host checks you off the reviewed guest list, hands you a NAME TAG, gets drinks moving. Nothing to download, no profile at the door.
sequence._name_tags: CONFIRMED by Taylor 2026-09-01: name tags ARE used. Both first-timer guides said 'No name tag' and were corrected. There is no scorecard -- that part was always right, and is worth keeping since it is the real contrast with speed dating.

sequence.step: Seated rounds, with the icebreaker game
sequence.detail: The room splits into balanced tables of about six, and a host-run game is what you play at the table -- that IS the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold. Round 1 everyone sits; every round after, women stay and men move one table along, so each round is an entirely new set of people.
sequence._moves: N seatings is N-1 moves. The default 4 x 15 is 3 moves and 60 minutes of tables.
sequence._icebreaker: CORRECTED 2026-09-01 by Taylor, who was asked directly. An earlier version of this record had the icebreaker as its own segment BEFORE the tables. It is not -- the game is played AT the tables, and the table structure is the icebreaker. That also explains why the dashboard has no icebreaker step: there is nothing separate to time. careers.html's 7:00 Icebreaker / 7:20 the actual evening split reads as two segments and should be re-read as round one (at the 20-minute setting) and the rounds after it.

sequence.detail: Go where you want. No structure, no host moving anyone -- by this point you have already met most of the room at the tables, so nobody is starting cold.
sequence._confirmed: Taylor, 2026-09-01, asked directly. It sits BETWEEN the seated rounds and the 1-on-1s. Not in the dashboard, because there is nothing to seat and nothing to time -- which is why reading the chemistry tool alone produced a run of show with this block missing.
sequence._this_is_what_the_old_copy_meant: The site's 'no whistle, no rigid rotation, conversations at your own pace' language was NOT invented. It describes this block accurately and then presents it as the whole evening. That is why the contradiction was so persistent: every party to it was half right. Copy should keep the at-your-own-pace idea AND say it is one movement of three.

sequence.detail: Rounds of simultaneous pairs, prioritising people you have not already shared a table with. A pair never repeats.
sequence._was_five: Hardcoded at 5 minutes until #379 (merged 2026-09-01) made it a host setting defaulting to SEVEN. Copy written before that -- including the first version of the listing pack -- says 'five-minute one-on-ones' and is now wrong. Like the seated rounds, this is a per-event choice, so listing copy must not state a number for it at all.

sequence.detail: Near the end, under a minute, nobody sees it but you.
Mutual interest becomes a match immediately, that same night.

run_of_show.timer: Wall-clock based, run by the host from a phone, one segment at a time. It stays correct if the screen sleeps.
run_of_show._safe_summary: Doors and drinks, then timed rounds at small tables with a game to break the ice and the men rotating one table each round, then open mingling, then 1-on-1s, then private interest notes and same-night matches. Three movements: structured, free, then paired. Say 'about four rounds of fifteen minutes' only if the host has confirmed the setting for THAT event -- both the count and the length are per-event choices.
_what_was_wrong: The blog and the city pages say 'no bell, no forced rotation, no seven-minute timer' and 'no rotation and no timer'. Flatly false against the shipped tool. Eight sentences across five files, still live as of 2026-09-01; scripts/build-listing-pack.js SITE_COPY_DEFECTS carries the list.

universal.landing_page_warning: CORRECTED 2026-08-23. The earlier version of this note read: '422 paid users -> ~10 begin_checkout -> ZERO purchases there, concentrated in the Facebook/Instagram in-app browser.' That evidence does not hold. /lp HAS NO CART AND NO CHECKOUT -- its Get Tickets button navigates to an event page. Zero purchases on /lp is the architecture, not a defect. The begin_checkout that produced the figure was mis-instrumented: before 2026-08-21 it fired on homepage and landing-page CTA TAPS, and #204/#229 corrected it to select_promotion for exactly this reason -- it was putting a funnel step on a page with no checkout and stitching together unrelated journeys. THE UNDERLYING CONCERN IS STILL LIVE, one page later: checkout runs on event.html via stripe.elements().create('card'), an embedded cross-origin iframe, and Meta/Instagram webviews restrict third-party storage. lp.html's own comment names the fix -- Stripe hosted Checkout, because what breaks is the embedded iframe, not top-level navigation. DO NOT GUESS AT IT: event.html already tags in_app_browser on checkout_form_started, checkout_3ds_required, checkout_3ds_completed, checkout_error and generate_lead. Segment checkout_form_started -> purchase by in_app_browser over a window starting 2026-08-22 or later, and that answers it. Corroborating signal already seen: checkout_error is 0 in webview against 5 in direct browser -- webview users are not failing at the card, they are not reaching it.

paid_template._comment: The paid counterpart to calendar_template, and a SEPARATE TABLE on purpose. Organic is a posting API -- one post, one timestamp, one row in queue.csv. Paid is the Marketing API -- a campaign with a lifecycle across a date range, carrying budgets, objectives and audiences. Forcing that into a row-per-post queue would put ads-manager fields on organic rows and a date range into a single-timestamp column. The DELIVERY is what differs. CORRECTED 2026-09-07: this note used to end 'The ART is still shared: paid creative that needs art emits queue rows so scripts/design-handoff.js picks it up unchanged.' That was never built and is not the plan any more. Paid creative does NOT emit queue rows -- it lives in playbook_v2.creative and is rendered by `scripts/build-paid-campaign.js --handoff`, the paid counterpart to scripts/design-handoff.js. Two briefs, one Claude Design; content/queue.csv stays organic-only.
paid_template._objective_and_gender_status: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 -- see playbook_v2 below, built from reports/ADS_OBJECTIVE_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-09-06.md section 8, and now the ONLY shape scripts/build-paid-campaign.js knows how to build (rewritten same day: 'I don't want to retain the old shape, I want the new playbook for go forward' -- Taylor, verbatim). The campaign/ad_sets/phases fields in THIS object (unchanged, below) are LEGACY, kept ONLY because Loxleys' one live campaign still reads them every night until it retires 2026-09-22 (memory lx-campaign-live) -- scripts/budget-ladder.js dispatches per registry entry on a `playbook` field: omitted or anything other than 'v2' reads campaign/ad_sets/phases below unchanged; `playbook: 'v2'` reads playbook_v2 instead. This is wind-down, not optionality -- no new event should ever set anything but `playbook: 'v2'`, and these legacy fields are safe to delete outright once Loxleys retires and nothing references them. Correction to a claim made when this was first flagged: content/paid-campaigns.json's `share` field was said to already support a two-campaign split with no change needed -- that undersold it. `share` is a flat fraction applied to every phase alike, but the playbook's cold:retarget ratio VARIES by phase (80/20 -> 60/40 -> 35/65), which a flat fraction cannot express. playbook_v2 uses a different registry shape instead (`role: 'cold'|'retargeting'`, both entries sharing the same `total`) -- see content/paid-campaigns.json's updated `_how_to_add`.

playbook_v2._comment: reports/ADS_OBJECTIVE_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-09-06.md section 8, the fully disambiguated build spec, adversarially verified. TWO campaigns per event -- cold and retargeting -- never one CBO campaign with gender-split ad sets. Rates below are PER DAY, not a percentage of a total to distribute: $10/$14/$16 over 7/7/8 days is the report's own reference event (~$296 total, the same band as Marion Court $221 and Tellus $234). A registry entry's `total` scales every phase's rate by total/reference_total_dollars -- see scripts/budget-ladder.js's roleRates().

campaign.one_per: event AND role -- build TWO campaigns, `<Event> | Cold` and `<Event> | Retargeting`, never one

campaign.attribution_spec: 7-day click, matching every ad set currently live

NEVER CBO here: learning_stage_info returned empty on all 4 live ad sets and pacing is already erratic at this volume (Marion Court's Sales campaign spending ~4% of its assigned budget) -- a CBO layer would let Meta silently override the cold:retarget split this playbook exists to enforce.

roles.targeting: broad, all genders, campaign geo -- PLUS the one exception in _gender_rule: a women-locked 2-for-1 cell inside this same campaign (genders:[2], gender expansion OFF, its own ABO budget), the only place the 2-for-1 creative runs. scripts/build-paid-campaign.js builds the broad set only; the cell is built by hand until it does.
video viewers + site visitors from the Cold campaign, all genders, 30-day custom-audience lookback
roles._why_live_from_seed: Seed's retarget leg is floor-spend insurance ($2.00/day, the Meta minimum) that keeps this campaign alive so it isn't a cold start when Build needs it to actually convert -- not real retargeting yet, since the pool barely exists at T-21.

playbook_v2._gender_rule: ONE gender-restricted ad set, and only one: the 2-for-1 cell. Rewritten 2026-09-10 -- Taylor's decision, option A of reports/TWO_FOR_ONE_TO_EVERYONE_2026-09-10.md -- after two of the 09-06 rule's four points were found not to hold. Every ad set is broad EXCEPT a women-locked cold ad set (genders:[2], targeting_automation.individual_setting.gender = 0 -- the expansion flag, checked separately from advantage_audience) that is the only place the 2-for-1 creative runs: never in the broad cold set, never in retargeting. WHY, measured on 44 delivered ads grouped by the gender Meta actually delivered to: every broad cold sales cell spent 60-68% on men (a woman's impression costs ~46% more, so an outcome-optimised auction drifts male; women's CPM was above men's in 21 of 22 ads); a women-locked cell lands 2.7x the women per dollar at the SAME cost per woman ($1.64 vs $1.61); the two times 2-for-1 copy reached men they clicked it at 83-96% of women's rate; and the +1 mirrors the buyer 7 of 7 -- a man shown the offer brings a man. Retargeting stays broad on a better reason than before: MC Retargeting, women-only, reached 407 people 11.67 times each for $103.14 and zero sales. RETIRED from the 09-06 text: 'a gender-restricted ad set cannot spend its budget' (a women-only set spent 101% of budget on 09-08; MC female close 2for1 spent $41.74 in four days) and 'men convert at the same rate per visit, so targeting buys nothing' (true and beside the point -- the lever is how many women visit per dollar). The n=6 correlation stays a caveat, not a basis. BUDGET: the cell is its own ABO ad set inside <Event> | Cold, funded out of the cold share, never below Meta's $2.00/day floor; the split inside cold is untested. NOT BUILT YET: scripts/build-paid-campaign.js builds one broad ad set per role and asserts genders undefined; playbook_v2.creative has no 2-for-1 creative. CHECKED: `npm run ads:review` lists every 2-for-1 ad that has ever reached men (under 97% of known-gender spend on women) and exits 3 when one is still delivering or when any ACTIVE ad set carries gender expansion; the two archived 2026-08 leaks stay on the record without failing every run.

phases.why: 80/20 is mechanically pinned to Meta's $2.00/day floor at $10/day total -- this isn't retargeting that converts yet, it's floor-spend insurance (see roles[].{_why_live_from_seed}).

Direction is measured (sales/retarget converts LPV->purchase at 1.9% vs sales/cold's 1.3%, and costs less per LPV: $1.25 vs $1.79); the exact 60/40 split is a judgment call inside that direction, on 4 vs 2 lifetime purchases.

Retargeting gets the majority in the harvest window (37% of historical ticket volume lands here). Cold never goes to zero -- the sales curve is backloaded enough that some event-day buyers haven't been touched by any ad yet.

playbook_v2._floor_priority_rule: If a role's computed daily amount would fall under Meta's $2.00 floor, that role is set to EXACTLY $2.00 and the OTHER role in the same phase absorbs the rest of the phase's total -- this is why Seed is $10/day and not lower; $10 is the smallest total where 20% lands exactly on the floor with no override. If a phase's scaled total would need to drop under $4.00/day to fund both roles past the floor, run cold-only for that phase and leave the Retargeting campaign's budget untouched rather than fund it below the floor. Implemented in scripts/budget-ladder.js roleRates() -- not a rule a human applies by hand.

_lead_time.status: informed_judgment, not measured -- this account's 6 historical first-ad lead times are 13/19/22/23/32/38 days (mean 24.5, median 22.5) and no event has ever actually launched at T-21, nor has any lead time been tied to a measured outcome. T-21 sits inside the real range, close to the median, and leaves one full week of Seed before the account's own measured final-14-day sales window opens.
_lead_time.cold_start_rule: If fewer than 21 days remain when planning starts, skip Seed and launch directly at Build's rate and 60/40 split. If fewer than 14 days remain, skip straight to Close's rate and 35/65 split. NEVER compress Close -- it's the single highest-value window by a wide margin. Implemented in scripts/budget-ladder.js phaseWindowsV2().

philadelphia_gate.status: MANUAL CHECKPOINT -- scripts/budget-ladder.js has no live Meta performance access and cannot make this call automatically.
philadelphia_gate.rule: Launch identically to Lancaster: Seed at $10/day, 80/20, broad. Hold at the Seed rate through the T-14 checkpoint -- do NOT auto-advance to Build or Close. At T-14, compare the Cold campaign's cost-per-landing-page-view against $2.70 (1.5x this account's $1.79 sales/cold benchmark). At or under: advance to Build and Close on schedule, identically to Lancaster. Over: hold at Seed's $10/day for the rest of the run rather than escalate spend into a setup that isn't responding.
philadelphia_gate.why_a_gate_not_a_different_template: Good Good already ran a HIGHER sales-objective share (56.9% vs Lancaster's 36.1%), heavier women-targeting (86.6%, the account's heaviest) and the LONGEST lead time (38 days) of any event, and still finished worst on every axis. If objective mix, gender mix or lead time were Philadelphia's problem, it should already be winning on one of those bases -- it isn't on any, so this playbook does not give Philadelphia a different structure, only a spend gate tied to a real in-flight number.
philadelphia_gate.n: Rests on n=1 (Good Good). A second gated Philadelphia event either confirms the gate is doing useful work or shows it needs recalibrating.

concurrent_event_rule.status: MANUAL DECISION -- the ladder's current behavior (refuse the whole run on a ceiling breach, see scripts/budget-ladder.js validate() and content/paid-campaigns.json guards.max_account_daily_dollars) is the safe default until this is worth automating.
concurrent_event_rule.rule: If two events' combined daily total would exceed the account ceiling, compress the EARLIER-PHASE event's Seed or Build budget first -- never a Close phase (T-7..T-0 carries 37-43% of historical ticket volume). If two events' Close phases would genuinely overlap, hold the smaller or later event at Build's rate one phase longer instead of running two Close budgets at once.

creative._comment: ADDED 2026-09-06. The one creative rule playbook_v2 has, made buildable: reports/ADS_OBJECTIVE_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-09-06.md section 8.3 -- 'Every phase's broad ad set should run that creative pattern [social-proof/testimonial] -- the lever is what the ad shows, not who it's aimed at.' The pattern is Taylor's own read (2026-08-25, memory social-proof-pulls-women): the Tellus AfterDark social-proof creative was the one campaign that converted women directly on the site. As of this date no ad on the account has ever carried a woman's testimonial -- the only testimonial creative live is Quang's (HANDOFF.md) -- so the three creatives below are three women's quotes from universal.approved_testimonials. Deliberately the SMALLEST block that lets `node scripts/build-paid-campaign.js --event=<KEY> --handoff` render one Claude Design brief for one event; it is not a general ad-copy system, and caption_templates (legacy, keyed by retired gender ad sets) is NOT its ancestor -- only its _voice and _slots notes are referenced.
creative._consumed_by: ONLY `node scripts/build-paid-campaign.js --event=<KEY> --handoff` (add --out=<file> to write it), which renders this block into a Claude Design brief -- one section per creative per role, with the slots filled from that event and every utm_content computed by scripts/ad-utm.js. That renderer landed 2026-09-07 and replaced the refusal this flag used to print. --execute does NOT read this block and must not: it builds two PAUSED campaigns with one broad ad set each and attaches no ad (its own docblock, 'WHAT THIS SCRIPT STILL DOES NOT DO'). Ads are attached SEPARATELY, after Design returns the videos, by the account's one proven attach path: scripts/meta-create-lx-sales-campaign.js lines ~443-468 -- POST /adcreatives with object_story_spec.video_data { video_id, image_hash, message, title, link_description, call_to_action } + url_tags from scripts/ad-utm.js, then POST /ads with { creative_id }, tracking_specs on the PURCHASE pixel, status PAUSED, then READ BACK url_tags because a 200 is not evidence. That script is hard-coded to Loxleys' gender ad sets; a v2 attach script reusing its request shape does not exist yet.
creative._rendition_id_trap: When an ad reuses an already-uploaded video, `creative.video_id` as returned by GET /adcreatives is a RENDITION id and is NOT the id to send. The real one is `creative.object_story_spec.video_data.video_id` (Loxleys female: 2549526178842057 rendition vs 1420196480082165 real; male: 1441913527996824 vs 1464886812146012). Diffing the rendition pair produced a wrong headline and a bad PR on 2026-09-02, and scripts/meta-create-lx-sales-campaign.js line ~49 carries the same warning. [The claim that a FIRST upload returns the real id directly, and that the trap only bites on reuse, is a reasonable reading of the two recorded pairs but was NOT tested on this account -- treat it as unverified and read the id back either way.]
creative._no_gender_axis: There is no gender key in this block. Creative maps onto ROLE (cold | retargeting), and the three testimonial creatives below run broad. The 2-for-1 creative is NOT in this block yet: per _gender_rule (2026-09-10) it runs only in the women-locked 2-for-1 cell, which scripts/build-paid-campaign.js does not build and this renderer does not know about. When it is added it needs its own entry with a gender axis (women) keyed to that cell -- the first and only such key -- not a fourth testimonial. Until then the female ad set that caption_rules.banned_outside_female_ad_set refers to is built by hand on the scripts/meta-create-lx-sales-campaign.js pattern (female ad set, gender expansion off, targeting read back). The 09-06 version of this note said that ad set 'no longer exists'; it existed on the live account throughout (Loxleys | female | Sales, Marion Court | Female | Sales) and is where every dollar of 2-for-1 spend has ever gone.

runs_in._note: ONE ad per creative per role, built on day one of Seed and left alone: report line 170 -- 'build both campaigns once, on day one of Seed, never recreate ... move between phases by editing daily budget only', and url_tags is frozen at creative creation (subcode 1815573). So the same ad runs Seed through Close and its copy MUST NOT state a fact that changes mid-run. That is why {price}, {early_price} and {early_through} are not in `slots` below: the early bird ends INSIDE the run on every event that has one -- T-15 on MC and LX, T-14 on TL2 (computed from events[].pricing.early_bird_through against events[].date; TL and GG carry no early_bird_through at all). A creative minted in Seed naming the early-bird price is quietly false for the whole of Close, the highest-value window in the cycle. That is the same defect PR #469 fixed on the organic side, where priceOf() served Marion Court's dead $18.99 two weeks after that price ended. Price belongs on the landing page, which is always current.

creative.format_ref: asset_rules.paid_ad_dimensions -- video 3-5s, silent-first, build feed_portrait 1080x1350 first, then feed_square and story_reel, plus one 1080x1350 still as the thumbnail (that still, uploaded to /adimages, is where the attach POST's image_hash comes from). Not repeated here; the handoff prints it from there.
creative._beats_exception: TWO deliberate departures from asset_rules.paid_ad_dimensions._beats, which the handoff prints verbatim. (1) Its 1-3s beat reads 'the facts (date, venue, doors, price)' -- the PRICE half does not apply here, per runs_in._note; date, venue and doors do. (2) Its 0-1s beat calls the hook 'the headline, large' -- here the hook frame is the QUOTE (see `hook` below), not the Meta headline, because the testimonial is the reason the ad works. Without this note a designer following the printed beats puts a price on a video that runs to T-0.
creative.voice_ref: paid_template.caption_templates._voice -- short declaratives, facts before pitch, no exclamation marks, no emoji. The testimonial QUOTE is verbatim and exempt: a quote that ends in an exclamation mark keeps it, because the punctuation is the speaker's and not ours. No quote text is reproduced in this block -- see _slots_note.
creative._slots_note: The first six are the subset of caption_templates._slots that stays true for the whole run (see runs_in._note). {quote} and {attribution} are new and resolve from universal.approved_testimonials by the creative's testimonial_id -- the quote text is NEVER typed here, so a corrected quote in that list corrects every rendered brief. {event_name} = events[].name, {venue}/{city}/{doors} verbatim, {date_long} as design-handoff.js's prettyDate renders it ('Tuesday, October 6'), {date_short} as the live Loxleys headline spells it ('Oct 6').
creative._hook_note: On-screen text for the 0-1s beat, large, because Meta autoplays muted (asset_rules.paid_ad_dimensions._silent_first). Molly's quote is 89 characters and will not read in one second; hold the hook frame longer inside the 3-5s cap rather than trim her words -- a shortened testimonial is a different testimonial.

copy._no_trailing_period_after_attribution: The attribution line ends with {attribution} and NO added period. Anonymous M.'s attribution already ends in one, and the earlier retargeting template appended a second -- '— Anonymous M..' rendered in the brief before this was caught on 2026-09-07. Any new copy here follows the same rule.
copy._note: Meta's three fields per ROLE, shared by every creative in `creatives` -- the quote varies, the pitch does not. cold introduces the event to someone who has never heard of it. retargeting drops the introduction (caption_templates.retargeting._no_reintroduction: re-introducing the event is how retargeting copy wastes its one advantage). Neither is keyed by phase -- see runs_in._note.

cold.primary_text:
“{quote}” — {attribution}, after a SparkDate night.

{event_name}. {date_long} at {venue}, {city}. Doors {doors}.

Not an app. Not speed dating. A room of people who decided to show up.
cold.headline: {city} · {date_short}

creatives._slug_why: The id has an underscore and scripts/ad-utm.js rejects one inside a slug (a separator inside a segment invents a field), so the slug is the id with it removed. Same person, same quote, attribution stays 'Anonymous M.' per her request.

creative._creatives_note: Each entry is one video asset: one person, one quote, whichever event -- all three are reusable_across_events. The slug is stable for the life of the account and lowercase [a-z0-9] only. If a creative is ever re-minted (a new dark post for the same quote, e.g. after a url_tags mistake), it needs a NEW slug (molly2), never the old one -- two creatives sharing a utm_content is the proof_rsa1 defect (caption_rules.utm._built_by). Three entries, three women, because that is the gap HANDOFF.md names; a man's quote is a fourth entry under the same two keys, not a schema change.
creative.asset_name_format: {event_key}-ad-{creative_slug}_{format_key}.mp4, plus {event_key}-ad-{creative_slug}_thumb.png -- e.g. TL2-ad-molly_feed_portrait.mp4. Paid creatives are not queue rows, so asset_rules.naming (row_id based) does not apply; this is the paid analogue and the handoff prints these names next to each render.
creative.utm_content: NOT DEFINED HERE, on purpose. The format lives at caption_rules.utm.content_format_v2 and is COMPUTED by scripts/ad-utm.js from this entry's `role` and `slug` -- pass {event, role, creative} and let it throw. An earlier draft of this block carried its own format string and role_tag map; that is a second definition of a rule ad-utm.js already owns, which is precisely how utm_content=proof_rsa1 reached thirteen delivered ads holding $554.39 (caption_rules.utm._built_by). Resolved 2026-09-07 by extending ad-utm.js to accept playbook_v2.roles[].key instead: it now emits <ev>_cold_<slug> and <ev>_rt_<slug>, refuses a role playbook_v2 does not define, and applies the same one-segment slug rule. tests/ad-utm.test.js gates it offline, including a case proving the v2 retargeting tag is byte-identical to the legacy one -- mc_rt_quang, live today, is already a valid v2 tag, so nothing built here splits from the ads running now.

_measured.read: 93 confirmed, non-comp tickets across 6 events, from Firestore on 2026-08-23.
_measured.basis: ONLY the 2 COMPLETED events (n=51). Events still on sale are CENSORED -- their late window has not happened yet, so including them biases the curve early. Loxleys' apparent 38-day median is that artifact, not a buying pattern. Re-measure after each event completes.
_measured._vs_playbook_curve: reports/ADS_OBJECTIVE_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-09-06.md's playbook reports 73% of tickets in the final 14 days / 37% in the final 7, cut across ALL 6 events including 2 still selling at pull time (Marion Court, Loxleys) -- exactly the censoring this file's own basis note above says produces an artificially early-looking curve. That figure was NOT reconciled against the 15/35/50 phase shares below, which were deliberately measured on only the 2 completed events for that reason. Re-run the playbook's sales-curve cut on completed events only before trusting either number over the other.
_measured.headline: 73% of tickets sell in the final 14 days. The last week alone (19 tickets) outsells everything before T-15 (14 tickets).
_measured.confidence: n=51 across two events, both Lancaster. Philadelphia has no completed event, so there is no market comparison. Treat the SHAPE as directional, not the percentages as precise.
_measured.early_bird_alignment: MC and LX both set early_bird_through at exactly T-15, which is where cumulative sales go 27% -> 55%. The price step and the volume surge already coincide. The budget step is placed there to match what already happens, not to invent a third schedule.

runway.compression: PROPORTIONAL, BUT ONLY ON THE PRIME PHASE.
runway._why: Buyer behaviour does not compress. People still buy in the final 14 days whether you advertised for 30 days or 21. Compressing every phase proportionally would move the budget step to T-10 on a 21-day runway and miss the real inflection at T-15. So prime absorbs all compression; step, convert, close and day_of stay anchored to absolute days before the event.
runway._floor: Below 18 days prime disappears entirely and retargeting launches with no audience pool. 21 days is the stated minimum for that reason.

_tiktok_ads.why: TikTok enforces a ~$20/day minimum per campaign. Total Meta spend across ALL FOUR events runs about $21/day ($530.76 over 25 days), so one TikTok campaign on one event would roughly double the entire ad budget, on a channel with no CPC history on this account. Windsor returns zero rows at 90 days.
_tiktok_ads.revisit_when: Daily Meta spend is comfortably above $50/day, so a $20/day test is a wing rather than a doubling.
_tiktok_ads.scope: ADS ONLY. TikTok ORGANIC continues unchanged -- it is free and already carries 17 of the 46 rows in content/queue.csv.
_tiktok_ads.if_resumed: Campaign -> Ad GROUP -> Ad, objective TRAFFIC, optimization CLICK, billing CPC, budget BUDGET_MODE_DAY. Those enums are Marketing API vocabulary and have NEVER been executed on this account -- confirm in Ads Manager. Windsor can pause/enable at all three levels and set budgets, but has NO create action, so the campaign must be built once by hand.
_tiktok_ads._lost_work: PR #262 built this as a full per-platform split of the campaign block. It was stacked on #261, and when #261 squash-merged GitHub auto-closed #262 as merged without its commit landing on main. The split is recoverable from branch claude/paid-per-platform if TikTok is ever resumed.

campaign.budget: CBO at campaign level, so Meta allocates between the gender ad sets instead of letting them bid against each other in separate auctions.
campaign.geo: The event's MARKET, from markets[].geo.cities -- a list of city+radius pairs, not one circle. Lancaster is Lancaster + Harrisburg + York at 20mi each; Philadelphia is one city at 15mi. Geography is a campaign property, not a matrix dimension: one campaign per event, not one per city-gender pair.
campaign._why_traffic: Measured on this account: LINK_CLICKS runs $0.13-$0.30 per click against $0.66-$1.58 for OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS on the same events. Established by #254 and #255.

ad_sets._offer_restriction: 2-for-1 COPY is female ads only. It is a MARKETING rule, not a product one: the offer itself is available to every buyer at checkout, on purpose (Taylor, 2026-09-02 -- gender-conditioned pricing at a public accommodation is the riskier legal shape, so the product treats everyone alike and only the advertising is aimed at women). A same-day attempt to gate it to women in the code was reversed for that reason. Never put it in male or retargeting copy.

ad_sets.offer: None in the copy. The offer exists at checkout for everyone; it is simply not advertised here.

ad_sets.targeting: video viewers and site visitors originating from the female and male ad sets
ad_sets._why_not_earlier: It has nothing to retarget until prime has built the pool. Launching it at T-30 produces a campaign with an empty audience -- which is exactly why Loxleys Retargeting was deliberately NOT built in #255.

paid_template._ad_set_note: Male and Female -- NOT 'All Genders' and 'Female'. The live account currently runs the latter, which targets women in BOTH ad sets so they bid against each other. That is the same pathology #254 fixed at campaign level, still present at ad-set level. Budget shares are a STARTING POINT and are NOT measured: female is weighted higher because gender balance is the binding constraint on these events, not because a test showed 45/30.

phases.action: Create the campaign and both gender ad sets PAUSED. Verify against the API afterwards rather than from the script's own output.
Link-click traffic on female + male. Cheap reach, and it builds the audience retargeting needs at T-14 -- it pays for itself twice.
Early bird ends and the price rises. Step the budget up to match -- this is the inflection, not an arbitrary marker.
Retargeting goes live. 27% of volume lands in this window.
Heaviest spend of the run. 37% of volume -- the single biggest window.

caption_templates._comment: LEGACY, AND RENDERED BY NOTHING (corrected 2026-09-07). Ad copy per ad set per phase, in Meta's three fields, keyed by the female/male/retargeting ad sets playbook_v2 retired -- see paid_template._objective_and_gender_status. This note used to claim 'scripts/build-paid-campaign.js renders these and scripts/design-handoff.js hands the rendered text to Claude Design'; neither is true. That script's --handoff renders playbook_v2.creative instead, and design-handoff.js has never contained a reference to this block -- it reads content/queue.csv and is organic-only. Kept for now only as the written record of the retired copy, and safe to delete with the rest of the legacy fields once Loxleys retires 2026-09-22. Its _voice and _slots notes are still cited by playbook_v2.creative and should move there if this block is deleted.
caption_templates._voice: Short declarative sentences and fragments. Concrete facts -- date, venue, doors, price -- before any pitch. No exclamation marks, no hype, no emoji. 'Not speed dating. Not an app.' is the register. Copied from the live organic captions, not invented.
caption_templates._phase_note: prime copy introduces the event to someone who has never heard of it. close copy assumes they have seen it and drops the explanation for the specifics. retargeting has no phase variants -- it only ever runs from `convert`, and by then everyone in the audience has already seen an ad.

Not an app. Not speed dating. A room of people who actually decided to show up.

Early bird {early_price} through {early_through}.

retargeting._no_reintroduction: This audience has already seen the event, so the copy does not explain it again. Re-introducing it is the most common way retargeting copy wastes its one advantage.

caption_rules._note: Every ad set needs its own caption. Male and female audiences are not reading the same pitch, and the 2-for-1 restriction makes a shared caption unsafe by construction. Retargeting copy assumes prior exposure -- it should not re-introduce the event from scratch.

utm._retargeting_why: Three segments, not four, and this is the rule the examples below always followed while the format string above said otherwise. For the retargeting ad set the phase and the audience are the same fact, so it is written once: mc_retargeting_retargeting_quang names nothing that mc_rt_quang does not. A retargeting ad also keeps its tag across convert and close, which is correct -- it is the same ad, and splitting one creative's clicks across two GA4 rows by phase would lose exactly what utm_content exists to preserve.
utm._v2_why: ADDED 2026-09-07 for paid_template.playbook_v2, whose axis is the ROLE (cold/retargeting) and which has no gender ad set to name. Three segments, and NO phase segment on purpose: under playbook_v2 the budget moves between Seed/Build/Close while the ad itself stays put, so a phase segment would split one creative's clicks across three GA4 rows -- the same loss `_retargeting_why` above already refuses for the legacy retargeting ad. role_tag collapses `retargeting` to `rt`, which has a useful consequence: `mc_rt_quang`, live today, is ALREADY a valid v2 tag, so nothing built under the new playbook splits from the ads running now. Computed by scripts/ad-utm.js from playbook_v2.roles[].key -- it refuses a role that block does not define, exactly as it refuses an unknown legacy ad set. Gated offline by tests/ad-utm.test.js, including a case asserting the v2 and legacy retargeting forms are byte-identical.
utm.content_case: lowercase snake_case, and each segment is one word: an underscore inside a slug invents a field, so 'show_up' is wrong where 'showup' is right. The event key is UPPERCASE in utm_campaign and lowercase in utm_content -- LX_202609 against lx_prime_female_showup. That asymmetry is live on the running Loxleys ads; changing either would split them from the ads built next, in the one field meant to join them.
utm._built_by: scripts/ad-utm.js computes all of this from these keys. Do not type a finished tag at a call site -- that is how utm_content=proof_rsa1 reached THIRTEEN delivered ads holding $554.39, 46% of everything the account has ever spent (reports/AD_ACCOUNT_AUDIT_2026-09-02.md). tests/ad-utm.test.js gates it in CI, which scripts/lint-ad-copy.js cannot: the linter reads live ads, needs a token, and only speaks after the creative exists -- by which time url_tags is frozen.
utm._source_why: Meta fills {{site_source_name}} per placement, lowercase (fb/ig/msg/an). Hardcoding it is how four ads spelled it 'facebook' and fourteen 'Facebook', which GA4 counts as two channels.
utm._content_why: This was '{ad_set_key}' until 2026-08-30, which names the AUDIENCE and not the AD. Two creatives in one ad set then share a utm_content and neither can be attributed -- the identical defect as 'proof_rsa1' on 11 ads, which scripts/lint-ad-copy.js raises as the account-wide 'utm-content-shared' ERROR. It also collided across events by construction: every future female prime ad would emit utm_content=female. Naming the event, phase, ad set and creative makes the value unique for the life of the account and readable as one GA4 row.
utm._immutability: url_tags is settable only when an AdCreative is CREATED (subcode 1815573). Getting this wrong at build time costs a new creative -- and a new dark post, forfeiting the running ad's likes, comments and shares. See scripts/check-meta-ad-tags.js.
utm._never_both: UTMs live in url_tags OR in the destination link, never both. Meta appends url_tags, so an ad carrying both sends two utm_source values and our code reads the first.

asset_rules.naming: {row_id}[_{subtype}][_{N}of{Total}].{ext}, row_id zero-padded to two digits (MC-02.jpg, TL-01_1of3.jpg, MC-12_story.jpg)
asset_rules._naming_note: Zero-padding matters: without it MC-10 sorts before MC-2 and the folder falls out of posting order.

paid_ad_dimensions._comment: Meta ad creative. Separate from the organic dimensions above: paid needs 4:5, which organic never used, and a paid Story ad needs no sticker safe-area because it carries no stickers.
paid_ad_dimensions._format: VIDEO, 3-5 seconds. The account ALREADY runs video ads -- the two Loxley's ads #255 built are named 'LX Women - Video Ad' and 'LX All Genders - Video Ad' and reuse video creatives. Stills were an error in the first version of the handoff.
paid_ad_dimensions._silent_first: Meta autoplays MUTED. Anything that must be understood has to be on screen as text; nothing may depend on audio. Assume the sound is never heard, because usually it is not.
paid_ad_dimensions._beats: 0-1s hook (the headline, large). 1-3s the facts (date, venue, doors, price). 3-5s the wordmark and a clear next step. Five seconds is not long enough for a story -- it is long enough for one claim plus the details that make it actionable.
paid_ad_dimensions._export: MP4, H.264, 30fps, under 30MB per file. Also export one still frame at 1080x1350 as the thumbnail: Meta shows it before playback starts and in placements that do not autoplay.

feed_portrait.note: 4:5 -- best-performing feed ratio, build this one first

story_reel.note: 9:16 -- keep the middle 80% clear of critical text

asset_rules._publish_format_note: Instagram's Content Publishing API accepts JPEG ONLY. Source exports are PNG in RGBA mode and cannot be handed to the API as-is; RGBA must be composited onto a background before JPEG encoding. TikTok also rejects PNG.

meta_ads._proven: #255 built campaign 120251072593050542 -- OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, CBO, two LINK_CLICKS ad sets and two ads -- through the Marketing API, verified against the API afterwards rather than from the script's own output.
meta_ads._utm_note: scripts/check-meta-ad-tags.js can REPORT missing UTMs but cannot write them: Meta rejects the url_tags parameter. UTM fixes are a manual paste in Ads Manager.
meta_ads._pipeline: Marketing API. Separate from the organic posting API in every way that matters -- a campaign is a lifecycle over a date range with budgets and audiences, not a post at a timestamp. This is why paid_template is its own table and not extra columns on queue.csv.

tiktok_ads.account: Ads account created 2026-08-23. Not yet connected to Windsor -- get_data returns 'No tiktok account for user'. Connect it before trusting any spend figure.
tiktok_ads.spark_ads: Promotes an existing organic post, but needs an ad authorisation code generated per post by the account owner, so it is not fully hands-off.
tiktok_ads._promote_button: TikTok's in-app Promote button is NOT the same thing as TikTok Ads. It has no public API and can never be scheduled -- if that is what is wanted, it belongs in the runbook's permanently-manual table.

ig._note: No scheduling parameter exists and media containers expire after 24h, so the container must be created at publish time by the runner.

ig_story._note: A Story can be posted via API but link and countdown stickers CANNOT be attached -- that is where the link and the urgency live, so sticker Stories stay manual.

tiktok.canvas: 1080x1920, and NOT the Story canvas: TikTok reserves the right ~250px for its action rail and the bottom ~380px for the caption, where Instagram reserves the top and bottom instead. Square 1080x1080 art posts but letterboxes. Render the vertical set with build-campaign-export --vertical; the -tt filename suffix is what routes it.
tiktok.token_lifetime: Access tokens last ~24h and are minted per run from TIKTOK_REFRESH_TOKEN. The refresh token ROTATES -- if the new value is not saved to the secret, publishing dies at the next run and needs re-authorising by hand.
tiktok._note: UPLOAD_TO_DRAFT works without TikTok's audit; DIRECT_POST requires a 2-4 week review. Photo posts (up to 35 images) are supported, so existing carousels can post with no new video. Unaudited apps are capped at SELF_ONLY, so DIRECT_POST before approval succeeds and posts privately to nobody -- run social-preflight for the real allowed privacy levels. PULL_FROM_URL also requires sparkdate.date to be verified in the TikTok developer portal.

x._note: Manual by decision (2026-08-21). The queue still writes caption_x so posting is a paste. X also killed its free tier for new developers in Feb 2026; pay-per-use is $0.20 per post containing a link, and every post here has one.
